title: Comparison of finite-field and prime-field Artin–Schreier character sheaves
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with $q=p^r$, where $p$ is prime and $r\geq1$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and put $L=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to L^\times$. For every nontrivial additive character $\psi:(k_0,+)\to L^\times$ there is a unique $b\in k_0^\times$ such that $\psi(c)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(bc))$ for all $c\in k_0$.

For this $b$, let $X$ be any separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Let $\pi_q:Y_q=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)\to X$, with translations $\sigma_c:y\mapsto y+c$ for $c\in k_0$, and let $\pi_{p,b}:Y_{p,b}=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[t]/(t^p-t-bf)\to X$, with translations $\tau_d:t\mapsto t+d$ for $d\in\mathbf F_p$. In the category of lisse $L$-sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], there is an isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{im}\left(\frac1q\sum_{c\in k_0}\psi(-c)\sigma_c:\pi_{q*}L\to\pi_{q*}L\right)
\ \simeq\
\operatorname{im}\left(\frac1p\sum_{d\in\mathbf F_p}\Psi(-d)\tau_d:\pi_{p,b*}L\to\pi_{p,b*}L\right).
$$
Here constant sheaves are denoted by $L$, and translations act by pullback. Thus the degree-$q$ Artin–Schreier sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] is the prime-degree $\Psi$-character sheaf for the function $bf$. The isomorphism commutes with pullback along morphisms of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes (with $f$ pulled back).

proof.text: Put chi = Psi composed with trace. Nondegeneracy of trace shows chi is nontrivial, hence primitive. Mathlib AddChar.to_mulShift_inj_of_isPrimitive makes its multiplicative-shift map injective. Distinct characters are linearly independent as functions on k, so the number of characters is at most |k|; the injective shift map therefore is bijective. Obtain the unique b with psi = chi.mulShift b. Nontriviality excludes b = 0, giving the required unit and uniqueness.

proof.text: Use the trace-cover theorem to obtain M, its translation-equivariant theta and its coordinate-preserving base-change maps. Map each explicit function cover to the universal Artin-Schreier cover by its root coordinate; this is a cartesian square. Transport the universal translation-transitivity assertion to these covers. For the prime cover use ULift (ZMod p) as the base field, with its structure map induced by the given prime-field algebra map; naturality of GammaSpecIso identifies its constants with those of M.

proof.text: On any geometric stalk of either finite cover, the finite stalk formula identifies sections with the product of the constant stalks over the fibre. Transitivity makes evaluation on a single point monic on the character-projector image, by the proved generic isotypic lemma. For surjectivity take the germ supported at that point, apply the projector and multiply by the order of the group: freeness kills every nonidentity summand and the identity summand evaluates to the original germ. Thus evaluation is an isomorphism. Freeness follows by mapping to the universal cover and using its translation-coordinate formula.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: character sheaves by pushout of the Lang torsor; agent-written trace-polynomial comparison with the prime-degree presentation

proof.text: Let phi be the prime-image inclusion followed by pullback of constant sections along theta. Equivariance of theta and the character identity make phi an eigenmap of character psi. Its adjoint along the q-cover is an isomorphism: on each geometric stalk, the constant-sheaf map calculus expresses it as prime-image evaluation at theta(s), followed by the canonical isomorphism between constant stalks. The generic isotypic descent criterion makes the induced map phi followed by the q-projector image factorization invertible after pullback to the q-cover. Surjectivity of that cover makes pullback reflect isomorphisms, producing e. The identity action of the projector on phi gives the required inclusion equation.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: character sheaves by pushout of the Lang torsor; agent-written trace-polynomial comparison with the prime-degree presentation

proof.text: The existing universal Artin-Schreier sheaf map to the pushed-forward constant sheaf has character psi and invertible adjoint. Apply the same generic isotypic descent criterion to the q-cover to identify artinSchreierSheafOf X psi f with its q-projector image. The existing lisseness theorem for artinSchreierSheafOf transports across this isomorphism and across e, proving both lisseness assertions. This uses the upstream universal-sheaf trivialization directly, without a new finite-etale local splitting or finite exchange argument.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: character sheaves by pushout of the Lang torsor; agent-written trace-polynomial comparison with the prime-degree presentation

proof.text: Use the trace-cover base-change clause for M prime. Its theta-equivariance follows by composing with the two legs of the prime-cover pullback square and applying its hom_ext. Construct e prime by the same fixed-cover comparison. Composition of pullback-of-sections maps proves the theta naturality square. Apply the same formula to every prime translation and sum to obtain projector compatibility. Finally use idempotence of the prime projector and the two inclusion equations to compute image(P) inclusion followed by the base map, the new image retraction, e prime and the new q-image inclusion; it equals e followed by the old q-image inclusion and its base map. This is the stated adjoint naturality equation.
